verses.1: David’s success was due to Jehovah’s help in carrying out the words of Kushba, my right-hand man.
verses.2: YHWH, my God, in you I place my trust. Save me from all my enemies and protect me.
verses.3: May it not be devoured like a lion; my soul is scattered, and there is no one to protect it.
verses.4: YHWH, my God! If I have done this, then surely there must be some reason for it.
verses.5: If I have done something wrong, then I hope that my enemies will be punished.
verses.6: He will devour my soul, tear it apart, and drag it back to the earth. My life and glory will be destroyed, and I will be buried in the depths of darkness.
verses.7: The LORD has come to you through His messengers. He has brought me before the judgment seat.
verses.8: And the congregation of the gods will abandon you, and they will return to their ruin.
verses.9: YHWH, you will judge the nations. YHWH, you will judge me with justice and fairness.
verses.10: May the wicked be destroyed, and may the righteous be honored. May God’s blessings be upon them.
verses.11: May God, the Savior of souls, be glorified.
verses.12: God judges the righteous and punishes the wicked every day.
verses.13: If his ruin does not return, then his ruin will be brought about through a certain process.
verses.14: And he prepared half of the things needed for burial, so that they could be used in funerals.
verses.15: Now, Yehabel-Auen and Hara Amal will give birth to a false child.
verses.16: He was buried and dug up, and he fell into the depths of destruction.
verses.17: Amal’s head will turn back, and on his forehead, there will be a mark.
verses.18: May the LORD be just, and may His name be praised.
